goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — throttle key is the raw embed_url, so trailing-slash/query/fragment variants of one article each get their own 60s budget and their own new topic: unbounded outbound fetches plus duplicate-topic spam

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 — the `TopicEmbed.where(...).exists?` pre-check is not a lock: a staff-triggered (no_throttle) retrieve racing the hourly PollFeed has both pass, and the loser's `TopicEmbed.create!` hits the unique index with an unhandled RecordNotUnique

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx and expire are not atomic, so a crash or failover between them leaves a permanent `retrieved:` key and that embed_url can never be retrieved again while loading.html reloads forever

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — the scheme guard uses `^` instead of `\A`, so a multi-line value such as "javascript:alert(1)//\nhttp://x/" passes the validation gate

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb` the URL scheme gate is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. In Ruby, `^` is a line anchor (can match after `\n`), and `=~` searches for a match anywhere in the string. So a multi-line value like `"javascript:alert(1)//\nhttp://x/"` would still match on the second line and bypass the intended scheme restriction. Using `\Ahttps?://` would correctly anchor to the start of the whole string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — URI(url).host` is `""` for `file://` URLs while embeddable_host defaults to `''`, so this host gate fails open rather than closed when the setting is unset

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when the param is absent, relying on Rails’ default exception handling to generate an error response (likely an HTML error page / generic 400). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — stray `end if` turns the header logo link into the if-modifier condition, reordering/altering the HTML every embed consumer receives

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — removal of the --category/-c option is an unannounced CLI contract break for existing import invocations

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.host/x.png`) match `start_with?('/')` and both slashes are stripped, producing the wrong absolute URL `http://host/cdn.host/x.png

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both `` and `` rewrite any `href`/`src` where the value `start_with?('/')` via `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError for feed items with no content element (RSS2 description-only), aborting the whole poll; nil `i.title` breaks import similarly

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:36 — check-then-act on `TopicEmbed.exists?` races the hourly PollFeed/other retrievals; the unique embed_url index makes the loser raise RecordNotUnique and abandon the rest of the feed

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple check-then-act paths around a unique `topic_embeds.embed_url` index. `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` does `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and then may trigger `Jobs::PollFeed` and/or `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, while `TopicEmbed.import` itself does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!` when blank. With concurrent retrievals (scheduled `PollFeed`, `RetrieveTopic` jobs, or `TopicRetriever` calling `PollFeed`), two workers can both see no row and then both attempt `create!`, causing `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. `PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` without rescue, so one such exception would abort the job mid-feed (and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means it won’t be retried).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — non-atomic setnx+expire: a crash between the calls leaves a TTL-less key that throttles that embed_url forever

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, throttling uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without a TTL, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return `true` forever for that embed_url (permanent throttle). This non-atomic pattern is verifiable in the diff and is a real correctness/availability defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — revise!`'s return/save result is ignored yet content_sha1 is updated, so a rejected revision is recorded as applied and the post never re-syncs

Since `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (it explicitly `return false if not should_revise?`) and the caller doesn’t check that result, the embed record can be marked as updated even if the post wasn’t actually revised. That would prevent future sync attempts because subsequent polls will see matching `content_sha1` and skip revising.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — a deleted topic leaves its TopicEmbed row, so TopicView raises NotFound permanently and no re-import is ever attempted

There is no per-item rescue, so a single bad feed entry will raise and abort the entire job, preventing later items from being processed in that run and likely causing repeated failures on subsequent hourly runs.

From the diff alone, there is no guarding around slow/unresponsive servers or very large feeds, so the Sidekiq scheduled job can block a worker thread/process for an unbounded time while reading the remote resource.

Since `poll_feed` performs network I/O via `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (and parsing) without any rescue, transient network/HTTP errors will cause the job run to fail and Sidekiq will not retry that run. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key is computed but never used, so the intended conditional-GET/dedupe mechanism is missing and the full feed is reprocessed hourly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) is run inline inside another job, doing a full blocking feed fetch and import on the user-triggered path.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does a blocking `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates/imports items. This is indeed running a full feed fetch/import inline within the embed retrieval path (which is invoked from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`), creating a performance/architecture concern (tying up a worker and potentially re-polling the entire feed per embed retrieval), though it’s not a directly verifiable correctness/security defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — An exception from the inline PollFeed propagates and skips the fetch_http fallback, so the article is never retrieved.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline and does not rescue any errors. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs network I/O (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and parsing (`SimpleRSS.parse`), either of which can raise; if an exception occurs, execution will abort before reaching the `fetch_http` fallback later in `perform_retrieve`, so the embed URL will not be retrieved in that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx followed by a separate expire is not atomic; a crash in between leaves a throttle key with no TTL, permanently blocking that embed_url.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two operations are not atomic; if the process crashes after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the throttle key will be created without a TTL, causing `setnx` to keep failing and the embed URL to be considered "retrieved recently" indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — The throttle key is claimed before retrieval and never cleared on failure, so a failed retrieval blocks retries for 60s while the loading page keeps reloading.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the Redis throttle key is set via setnx/expire before perform_retrieve runs. If perform_retrieve/fetch_http raises (e.g., TopicEmbed.import_remote uses open(url).read with no rescue), the key will still remain until its 60s TTL expires, preventing another retrieval attempt during that window. This matches the finding’s behavior, but it appears to be an edge-case/UX concern around throttling semantics rather than a hard correctness break, since the key does expire and retries will eventually happen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read has no timeout, redirect or size limit and no rescue for OpenURI/socket errors.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) without specifying `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, without limiting response size, and without handling network/redirect-related exceptions. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:34 — The update path is outside Topic.transaction, so a failure between revise! and update_column leaves content and content_sha1 inconsistent.

If `revise!` succeeds and `update_column` fails/raises (DB error, connection issue, etc.), the post content is updated but `topic_embeds.content_sha1` remains stale, leaving the embed record inconsistent with the post content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — revisor.revise! return value is ignored and content_sha1 is updated regardless, so a failed revision is recorded as applied and never retried.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when `content_sha1` differs it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The diff also shows `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (early `return false if not should_revise?`) and `update_post` relies on `@post.save(...)` which can return `false` (lib/post_revisor.rb). Since the result isn’t checked, a failed/aborted revision could still advance `content_sha1`, leaving the embed marked up-to-date even if the post wasn’t revised, preventing future retries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — embed.post can be nil if the post was deleted, making PostRevisor.new(nil) raise and abort the poll.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then, when content changes, immediately calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` without guarding against `post` being nil. Since the migration creates `topic_embeds.post_id` without a foreign key constraint and there is no `dependent:`/cleanup behavior shown, an existing TopicEmbed row can remain after its Post is deleted, making `embed.post` nil and causing an exception that would break the feed poll/import flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:23 — If creator.create returns nil the TopicEmbed row is silently not created and no error is raised, so the url is retrieved again on every request.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when `embed.blank?` it calls `creator = PostCreator.new(...)` then `post = creator.create` and only creates the `TopicEmbed` record inside `if post.present?` (so a nil/blank post results in no `TopicEmbed` row and no explicit error handling). However, the finding’s consequence is overstated: requests won’t necessarily “retrieve again on every request” because retrieval is throttled in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` via Redis (though `EmbedController#best` will still enqueue a job whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns nil). This is a real edge-case/robustness concern, but not a directly verifiable defect without knowing when/if `PostCreator#create` can return nil.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:25 — Concurrent imports of the same url (scheduled poll plus inline retrieve) race on the unique embed_url index and raise RecordNotUnique, aborting the caller.

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. With the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`), concurrent callers can both see `embed.blank?` and race to `create!`, causing `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` to be raised and not rescued. The diff also introduces multiple concurrent entry points (`Jobs::PollFeed` scheduled job and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever`), making this race plausible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — Non-http urls are dropped silently with no logging, hiding partial feed import failures.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the first line is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which will silently return `nil` for non-http(s) URLs with no logging or error reporting. Since callers like `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` iterate items and call `TopicEmbed.import(...)` without checking/logging the return value, some feed entries could be skipped without any visibility. This is an observability/diagnostics concern grounded in the diff, not a strictly verifiable correctness defect given no stated requirement to import non-http(s) links or to log skips.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The page reloads every 30s forever with no attempt cap or error state, looping indefinitely when retrieval never succeeds.

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb, the only behavior is a `setTimeout` that calls `document.location.reload();` every 30000ms with no max retry or fallback UI. If the background job never succeeds (e.g., network error, invalid URL, or other failure in `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` / retrieval), the iframe will keep reloading indefinitely, causing a poor UX and unnecessary repeated requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute caches the loading page for 60s, so the 30s reload can be served the cached loading page and miss the ready topic.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed regardless of whether a topic was found or the `loading` template was rendered. When no topic exists yet, the controller enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading`, but that loading response will also be cacheable for 60s. Since `loading.html.erb` triggers a reload after 30s, an intermediary cache or the browser can legitimately serve the cached loading page for up to the full minute, delaying discovery of the newly-created topic and potentially causing repeated cached loading responses until expiry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — A Jobs.enqueue failure (Redis/Sidekiq down) raises a 500 inside the iframe instead of degrading gracefully.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it unconditionally calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and then renders `loading` (new code around lines ~12-18). There is no `rescue`/fallback if `Jobs.enqueue` raises (e.g., Sidekiq/Redis client errors), so an exception would bubble up and the iframe request would return a 500 instead of the intended loading UI. This is a robustness/operational edge case rather than a guaranteed functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — create_table :topic_embeds, force: true drops an existing table on re-run, destroying embed mappings.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` in `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table before creating it, so if this migration is rerun (e.g., `db:migrate:redo` or if the table already existed for any reason) it would destroy existing `topic_embeds` data/mappings. However, as a new migration adding a new table, this is not a defect in the normal one-time forward migrate path; it’s a risky practice/data-loss hazard rather than a currently triggered bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — force: true was added to an already-shipped migration, so re-running it drops existing top_topics data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which in Rails will drop and recreate the `top_topics` table if it already exists when this migration is executed. That introduces a data-loss risk on re-running this migration (e.g., in environments where the table exists but the migration runs again).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:147 — import_remote is called per thread with no rescue or timeout, so one unreachable link aborts the whole import with no resume.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Disqus import task to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` for each thread (lib/tasks/disqus.thor). `import_remote` performs `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) with no timeout options and no exception handling; the call site in the loop also has no `begin/rescue`. Any network error (unreachable host, timeout, invalid response) would raise and terminate the entire import, preventing continuation with remaining threads—this is a real failure mode introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — @post.save(validate: false) return value is ignored, so a failed save during embed updates passes silently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` and still ignores the boolean return. In the new embed update path (`TopicEmbed.import` calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true)`), a non-exception save failure (e.g., callback abort) would not be detected, yet `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` would still run, risking an inconsistent embed record vs. post content. However, the diff does not prove such a failure will occur (and save return was also ignored before), so it's a robustness concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Raw RSS item content is unescaped with CGI.unescapeHTML and imported verbatim with no HTML sanitization, yielding stored XSS once rendered

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed item HTML is taken from `i.content` (after `CGI.unescapeHTML` and `.scrub`) and passed to `TopicEmbed.import` without any sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This combination makes stored XSS from malicious RSS/Atom content directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — raw post.cooked` renders post HTML unescaped, and for raw_html posts cooked is unsanitized remote article/feed HTML, so arbitrary script runs on the Discourse origin

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook method where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim (`app/models/post.rb`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` without any sanitization of `contents` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Feed polling pulls `i.content` from an external RSS/ATOM feed (`Jobs::PollFeed`) and passes it through `CGI.unescapeHTML` but does not sanitize/strip scripts before importing. In the embed view, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders `raw post.cooked`, and for `raw_html` posts `cooked == raw`, so arbitrary HTML from the feed/article is emitted unescaped and can execute script in the Discourse iframe origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — cook() returns raw verbatim for cook_method raw_html, completely bypassing the sanitizing markdown pipeline for these posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `Post.cook_methods` with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking/sanitizing pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`). This mode is then used for externally sourced content (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import` via RSS/Readability sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). Since RSS content is taken largely verbatim (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`), and Readability output is not shown to be sanitized by Discourse here, this can result in untrusted HTML being rendered without sanitization (XSS risk).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — Feed-supplied url is interpolated into a single-quoted href attribute without escaping, allowing attribute break-out/HTML injection (only an ^https?:// prefix check is applied)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends `"#{url}"` into `contents` with only a `^https?://` regex check (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`). A feed-supplied `url` can legally contain a single quote (or other HTML-significant characters) while still matching that prefix, which would break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and inject arbitrary HTML/JS. This is especially impactful because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and later rendered with `raw post.cooked`, so the injected markup would be served unescaped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote passes an externally-influenced URL to Kernel#open (open-uri) with no scheme/IP/redirect restrictions, enabling SSRF (and command execution for a leading `|` if the host check is ever bypassed)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the diff introduces `open(url).read` on a URL that ultimately comes from external input paths (e.g., `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` with `embed_url` from params; `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` passes it to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). There are no scheme/IP/redirect restrictions in `import_remote` itself. Even though `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks `URI(@embed_url).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, `open-uri` can follow redirects to other hosts/IPs, enabling SSRF despite an initial host check. Additionally, `import_remote` lacks any `http/https` scheme enforcement and uses `Kernel#open`; a leading `|` would be treated as a command by `Kernel#open` if reachable (and `import_remote` is also called from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` with `t[:link]`, which is not shown as strictly trusted). This is a concrete security issue grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Embed authorization relies solely on the Referer header host, which is trivially forged by non-browser clients and stripped by referrer policies

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` gates access solely by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and then sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`. The diff shows no additional authentication/nonce/signature, so a non-browser client can trivially bypass the host restriction by sending a forged `Referer` header, and legitimate embeds can also fail when the referrer is omitted/stripped (treated as invalid and rejected).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — X-Frame-Options is set to ALLOWALL, removing framing protection for this response for every origin rather than only the embeddable host

adjudication.rationale: The diff does set `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, which disables browser-enforced framing restrictions for this endpoint. However, the same method gates access by requiring `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, so other origins generally cannot load/frame the response in a browser. The finding is therefore a valid hardening/defense-in-depth concern (header is broader than necessary), but it’s not a clearly exploitable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Unauthenticated GET with an arbitrary embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job that makes an outbound fetch, allowing job-queue flooding and server-side request amplification

adjudication.rationale: EmbedController#best enqueues `:retrieve_topic` whenever no existing TopicEmbed is found (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)`), and there is no authentication check shown in this diff. The only gate is `ensure_embeddable`, which relies on `request.referer` matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`—a header that can be spoofed by non-browser clients—so it doesn’t reliably prevent unauthenticated callers. The job ultimately performs outbound network access via `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and can also trigger `Jobs::PollFeed` which calls `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates items. Throttling in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is per-URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so an attacker can flood the queue by varying embed_url (e.g., querystrings) and force repeated outbound fetch work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — postMessage targetOrigin is built from the untrusted Referer (full URL, not an origin) and interpolated into inline JS; empty/odd referers break the origin restriction

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the code calls `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `request.referer` is a full URL (including path/query) and can also be blank/odd; `postMessage`’s `targetOrigin` is supposed to be an origin (scheme+host+port) or `"*"`. Passing a full referer URL means the browser’s origin check won’t match (or may error for invalid/empty), so the resize message can fail and the origin restriction is effectively mis-specified. This is directly introduced by the new inline JS in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — Feed polling opens an admin-configured URL via open-uri with no scheme allowlist, timeout, or size limit (SSRF/DoS)
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that the job uses open-uri to fetch an admin-configured URL without validation/allowlisting, which enables SSRF (fetching arbitrary internal/external URLs). Extra mentions of timeout/size limits (DoS) are additional concerns but the core issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — postMessage origin validation uses a loose `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` substring test and no e.source check instead of an exact origin comparison
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: origin validation is done with a substring `indexOf` check rather than an exact origin match, which can be bypassed by attacker-controlled domains that contain the trusted URL as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com). It even adds an extra related concern (missing e.source check), but the primary issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — No explicit guardian/visibility check before building the TopicView, so embedded topics in restricted categories may be exposed to anonymous users if TopicView does not enforce it

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `topic_id` is found it directly does `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with `current_user` potentially `nil` (anonymous) and without any explicit authorization/visibility check in this controller (the only gate shown is `ensure_embeddable`, which validates the referer host and sets `X-Frame-Options`). Whether restricted topics can actually be exposed depends on `TopicView`/downstream guardian enforcement, which is not shown in the diff, so the security impact can’t be verified here—but the lack of an explicit check in the newly added embed endpoint is a concrete, diff-grounded concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:33 — perform_retrieve and retrieved_recently? are both stubbed in every test, so the retriever's real work (existing-embed bail-out, feed fallback, fetch_http, redis throttle) has zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the “valid host” examples stub retrieved_recently? (returns false/true) and only assert whether perform_retrieve is called, while the “invalid host” examples mock perform_retrieve to never run. No test exercises TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve’s real branches (existing embed bail-out via TopicEmbed.where(...).exists?, feed fallback via Jobs::PollFeed when feed_polling_enabled?, or fetch_http/import_remote), and the redis throttle behavior in retrieved_recently? is never executed. The finding overstates “both stubbed in every test”, but the core point—zero coverage of the real work paths introduced in lib/topic_retriever.rb—is accurate and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:35 — poll_feed is stubbed in all four tests; the actual feed parsing, link/id fallback, unescaping and TopicEmbed.import call are never executed, so the feature could be entirely broken with a green suite

adjudication.rationale: The spec in spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only exercises Jobs::PollFeed#execute guard conditions and that it delegates to #poll_feed (via expects(:poll_feed).never/once). It never runs the real #poll_feed implementation added in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb (SimpleRSS.parse open(...), link/id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and TopicEmbed.import), so those behaviors could regress without failing tests. The finding’s wording about “stubbed in all four tests” is slightly off (it’s expectations on calls rather than stubbing), but the underlying coverage gap is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 — import_remote has no test at all despite being the entry point used by TopicRetriever#fetch_http and disqus.thor

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds TopicEmbed.import_remote (app/models/topic_embed.rb) and it is used by both TopicRetriever#fetch_http (lib/topic_retriever.rb) and the Disqus Thor task (lib/tasks/disqus.thor). However, the newly added specs only cover TopicEmbed.import (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb) and TopicRetriever.retrieve control flow (spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb), and do not exercise import_remote’s behavior (Readability parsing, open(url).read, allowed tags/attributes, passing title/content into TopicEmbed.import). This is a specific missing-test gap for a new entry point used in production flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 — import_remote calls open(url) but topic_embed.rb only requires nokogiri (open-uri is required in poll_feed.rb); no test exercises this load path so a NameError/missing-require would ship undetected

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but this file only `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` and later `require 'ruby-readability'`; it never requires `open-uri`. In Ruby, without `require 'open-uri'`, `Kernel#open` won’t handle HTTP URLs (it will attempt to open a local file like `http://...`), so `import_remote` can fail at runtime. The diff also shows `open-uri` is required only in `poll_feed.rb`, which doesn’t guarantee it’s loaded before `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (e.g., the Disqus thor task now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). No spec covers `import_remote`, so this failure path wouldn’t be caught by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — no test asserts X-Frame-Options is absent/unchanged when ensure_embeddable rejects the request, so a bypass of the frame protection would go unnoticed

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` is set only after the host/referer checks pass, and the spec only asserts the header in the success path (`after` block in `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`). The failure-path tests (missing host, no referer, etc.) only assert `response.should_not be_success` and do not assert that `X-Frame-Options` remains unset/unchanged when access is rejected. That’s a specific, diff-grounded test gap around newly added framing behavior, not a demonstrable defect in the current implementation.
